text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
author: Isaac Newton

text: I can calculate the motion of heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people.
author: Isaac Newton

text: Truth is ever to be found in simplicity, and not in the multiplicity and confusion of things.
author: Isaac Newton

text: Nature, to be commanded, must be obeyed.

author: Francis Bacon

text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.

text: Chance favors the prepared mind.
author: Louis Pasteur

text: We have a hunger of the mind which asks for knowledge of all around us.
author: Maria Mitchell

text: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.

text: I have not failed. I have just found ten thousand ways that will not work.

text: Opportunity is missed by most people because it is dressed in overalls and looks like work.

text: There is no substitute for hard work.

author: Galileo Galilei

author: Thomas Huxley

author: Thomas Huxley

text: The known is finite, the unknown infinite.
author: Thomas Huxley

author: Galileo Galilei

text: Mathematics is the queen of the sciences.

author: Voltaire
